title: Unbounded derived global sections
statement:
For a scheme $T$ and a commutative ring $\Lambda$, use the category $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$, and its unbounded derived category $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Given $K\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, choose a cochain complex $C$ representing $K$ and a K-injective resolution $C\to I$ in this module-sheaf category [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], which exists by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For a module sheaf $M$, put $\Gamma(T_{\Et},M)=M(T)$ with its $\Lambda$-module structure [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; this is sections at the terminal object, as in [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor], applied termwise to complexes. Define

$$
\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)=\Gamma(T_{\Et},I)\in D(\Lambda),
\qquad
H^q(T_{\Et},K)=\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(T_{\Et},K))\quad(q\in\mathbf Z),
$$

where the complex of sections is viewed in the derived category of $\Lambda$-modules and $\mathcal H^q$ is its cohomology module [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Independence of the chosen representative and resolution is recorded with the other properties of this construction. For $K\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], agreement with the bounded-below K-injective recipe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], carried out in $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, is also recorded there. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ this is exactly that abelian-sheaf definition; for general $\Lambda$ the resolutions and sections in the recipe retain their $\Lambda$-module structures.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported definition against its blueprint, dependencies, and the slopmaster2 source. The source declarations rightDerivedGlobalSections and cohomology are generic functors for any Grothendieck abelian coefficient category; they do not state the item’s explicit commutative-ring K-injective-resolution construction, so the earlier attachment was rejected. The definition is split with no new nodes because all three notions it cites already exist in the DAG. Maintainer review clarified the representing complex, module-valued termwise sections, D(Lambda) and its cohomology, adding their existing definition dependencies. The bounded-below reference is explicitly the same recipe in module sheaves, literally the cited abelian-sheaf definition when Lambda=Z.
